kind: quiet, realization
pov: Dorren Hayle

Dorren laid the old survey over the new one and pinned both corners. The river
bent where it had always bent. The ridgeline held. She ran the calipers from
the fork to the ford, read the scale, and ran them again.

Thornwick should have been there, a cluster of six inked squares and a mill.

She checked the scale bar twice. The village was not there.

Behind her the press went on clanking two floors down, and somebody asked for
a second opinion on a contour. She did not turn around. She wrote the
discrepancy in the margin, in the small square hand the office required, and
dated it.
